- Target P95 latency: <= 350ms for streaming chat responses (end-to-end)
- Sustained throughput target: 800 requests/minute (mixed traffic: 60% chat, 40% embeddings)
- Concurrency: peak 120 concurrent sessions (chat ws connections using streaming)
- KV cache expectations: cold-start acceptable for first 5 minutes; afterwards we expect cache hit > 80%

Next steps / asks from Acme: 
1) Provide a k6 or Locust script we can run (customer-led) – you mentioned you prefer k6.
2) We'll provision a test account + API key and an IP allowlist so your infra can run tests from your VPC.

I've looped in Marissa (solutions eng) and Aditya (SRE/runtime) to share the k6 template, IP ranges, and test account details. I attached an initial k6 script and allowlist template for your team to adapt.

If any of the targets above need to shift before we run tests, let me know by EOD today and we'll adjust the scenario.

Thanks,

Hi Tom – attaching a lightweight k6 script (acme_k6_script.js) that emulates a mixed workload (chat streaming + embeddings). Key notes: 

- k6 websocket support: k6 supports websockets via the ws module (we include an example connection that sends a prompt and listens for chunked messages). If you prefer Locust, I can paste a minimal Locustfile as well.
- Streaming accuracy: the script simulates chunked responses by reading the event stream; however, we recommend focusing on end-to-end latency per message (time-to-first-chunk and time-to-last-chunk) rather than raw throughput for streaming checks.
- Authentication: the test API key will be scoped to a sandbox project with no cross-tenant access. Keys are single-purpose and can be rotated/revoked immediately after tests.
- Rate limiting: tests will be allowed to exceed normal production rate limits for the duration of the scheduled window (we'll apply a test quota). Please still respect our suggested ramp to avoid unexpected overload during warm-up.

Attachments included: acme_k6_script.js (k6 example), ip-allowlist-template.txt (format for adding your CI egress IPs), test-account-instructions.pdf (how to use the sandbox key + endpoints).

Example k6 snippet (high level):
- setup(): fetch model list + warm KV cache
- default function: open websocket, send prompt, await streamed chunks, capture latency metrics (ttfc, ttlc), close connection
- thresholds: p95(ttfc) < 350, p95(ttlc) < 1.2s for chat; iterations/second target to meet 800 rpm overall

I'll be available Wednesday morning if you want to run through the script live.

–Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
